research_crypto.verdict:
One finalist passes the pre-registered criteria, but weakly; the other fails. I do not consider the pass strong enough to plan growth on.

PASSES (letter of PROTOCOL_V2, both sleeves and the basket): brk72_24h_wd, a weekday 72-hour close-channel breakout on H1 bars with a fixed 3 x ATR stop and a 24-hour exit, on BTCUSD and ETHUSD. In-sample PF 1.78 / 1.67 (t 4.6 / 4.2). Validation 2022-2025: PF 1.084 / 1.134, expectancy +0.041R / +0.064R, t 0.77 / 1.20; basket PF 1.108, t 1.38; 2025 negative (BTC -18.1R, ETH -1.3R).

Why it is marginal: the per-trade edge fell 83% from in-sample to validation and is now about the size of its costs. BTC earns +3.4 bp gross per trade against about 7 bp of costs and is positive only in R terms (net -4 bp per trade, equal-size PF 0.96). ETH earns +12.7 bp gross against about 11 bp. Two extra basis points of round-trip cost put BTC exactly at the PF 1.06 bar, and the FP crypto spreads are still provisional. BTC also cannot be sized prudently on 1,000 EUR: the minimum lot risks 14.3 EUR (1.4%) per trade. If anything is kept, keep ETH only, at small weight (about 0.45 trade a day).

FAILS: sess_8_8_13_wd (Asia-session direction held from 08:00 to 21:00 UTC, weekdays). It passed every in-sample criterion (PF 1.43 / 1.40) and fails validation (PF 1.032 / 1.047).

Short-horizon crypto momentum was very strong in 2017-2020, flat per signal in 2021, and barely above costs since. Nothing on this track delivers several trades a day or fast growth.

finalists.name: brk72_24h_wd
finalists.rule: Sleeves: BTCUSD and ETHUSD, one position per sleeve. Bars: H1 on the UTC hour grid (identical to MT5 server H1 bars), mid prices (MT5 bid closes are equivalent up to half a spread); 'bars' means existing H1 bars, hours without quotes are skipped. At the scheduled end of every H1 bar (first tick of the next hour), if that instant is Monday-Friday in UTC and no trade of the sleeve is open at that instant (a trade whose time exit is due at this same instant still counts as open, so the signal is ignored): let C = close of the bar just finished. LONG at market if C is above the highest close of the 72 bars before it; SHORT at market if C is below the lowest close of those 72 bars; otherwise nothing. Drop the signal if no quote arrives within 5 minutes after the bar end. Stop-loss: 3 x ATR24 from the fill price, where ATR24 = arithmetic mean of the true ranges of the last 24 completed H1 bars including the signal bar (MT5 iATR(H1,24) at shift 1), frozen at the decision; no target, no trailing, no break-even. Time exit: close at market at the first tick at or after decision time + 24 hours. Sizing: fixed fraction of equity risked per trade (lots = risk money / stop distance).
finalists.basket: Declared before validation (pooled BTC+ETH trades, same parameters). IS: n 1215, PF 1.727, t 6.16, expectancy +0.299R, 5/5 years (2021: +27.5R), cost-stress PF 1.697, every-signal expectancy +0.283R -> pass. VAL: n 1319 (331 a year), PF 1.108, expectancy +0.0517R, t 1.38, 3/4 years (2022 +29.6R, 2023 +25.7R, 2024 +32.3R, 2025 -19.4R), max drawdown 37.4R, cost-stress PF 1.084, every-signal expectancy +0.068R, expectancy positive on each instrument -> pass.

Passes the pre-registered criteria on both sleeves and as a basket, but the validation evidence is weak: t 0.77 (BTC), 1.20 (ETH), 1.38 (basket); a weekly block bootstrap of the validation trades gives P(mean R > 0) of 77% for BTC and 90% for ETH. BTC/ETH weekly-R correlation in validation is 0.64, so the two sleeves are about 1.2 independent bets.

Decay: gross edge per trade on BTC went 92 bp (first half of IS) -> 43 bp (second half) -> 23 bp (2021) -> 3.4 bp (2022-25), against about 7 bp of costs. ETH went 76 -> 58 -> 17 -> 12.7 bp against about 11 bp. BTC is positive only in R terms: net -4.0 bp per trade and equal-size PF 0.96. BTC 2025: -18.1R, with the last three quarters all negative.

Cost cushion (arithmetic on the saved validation trades): +2 bp of extra round-trip cost puts BTC at PF 1.06 and +7.3 bp at break-even; ETH breaks even at +15 bp. The FP crypto spreads in fp_costs.json are provisional.

Weekday filter: adopted before validation but after seeing an in-sample split. The data has no weekend quotes in 2017-18 and partial ones in 2019-20, and weekend decisions in 2019-21 earned about zero. The in-sample numbers of this form are therefore slightly flattering; the all-days form had IS PF 1.54 / 1.61 (t 3.8 / 4.2) and was never run on validation.

Other in-sample caveats: 2017-18 trades whose exit waited for the weekend reopening of the feed made about +1R each; without all closure-delayed exits IS is still PF 1.67 / 1.63, t 3.96 / 3.94. In 2021 the every-signal run was flat on both instruments (BTC +8.8R on 703 signals, ETH -1.8R on 709).

Checks done: truncation test identical on 36 cuts per sleeve; an independent bar-by-bar re-implementation matches the engine on every trade of two in-sample slices; sending the order 5 or 30 minutes late leaves the in-sample PF at 1.51-1.56 (measured on the all-days form).

Defaults in force: atr_n 24, max_delay_min 5, both sides.

My planning numbers: probability that the after-cost edge is positive going forward about 55% for ETH and 45% for BTC; expectancy +0.02R to +0.04R per trade; about 0.45 trade a day per instrument.

research_crypto.engine_concerns:
1. Extra order columns silently overwrite engine output columns (this bit me). `sim.simulate` copies every non-standard order column into the trades frame before swap, hold and R are computed. A column named `exit_time` (also `entry_time`, `entry`, `exit`, `reason`, `mfe`, `mae`) replaces the engine's value. My first 26 trials carried a scheduled-exit column called `exit_time`, so swaps were charged up to the scheduled exit and holds were overstated (pessimistic, large for trailing exits). Minimal repro on 2021 data:

    m1 = r2.load("btcusd", start="2021-03-01", end="2021-03-12")
    o = pd.DataFrame({"entry_i": [100], "side": [1], "stop_dist": [150.0], "exit_i": [12000]})
    gl.simulate(m1, o, sym="btcusd", costs=r2.costs("btcusd"))                                   # stop after 162 min, swap 0, R -1.05
    gl.simulate(m1, o.assign(exit_time=m1.index[12000]), sym="btcusd", costs=r2.costs("btcusd")) # hold 11,907 min, swap 205.7 USD, R -2.42

Workaround: column renamed to `sched_exit`; the 18 breakout configurations were re-run and logged again.

2. Time exits and closures. I use "first M1 bar at or after the scheduled exit" (what a live EA does) rather than `gl.exit_index`. In the 2017-2018 data, which has no weekend quotes, Friday trades therefore exit at the Sunday reopening. Those trades made about +1R each: 31 BTC and 14 ETH breakout trades, 41 and 27 session trades. Every sleeve still passes in-sample without all closure-delayed exits (t 3.4-4.0). Validation has none (max hold 24.4 h).

3. Data quality in-sample (details in data_check.json).
- BTC starts 2017-05-07, ETH 2018-01-01. No weekend quotes before 2019; weekends are complete only from 2021. Minutes present: BTC 66% (2017), 69% (2018), 93-94% (2019-20), 99.5% (2021); ETH 66%, 77%, 88%, 99.5%.
- BTC quotes in May-September 2017 bounce: 1,950 one-minute bars with a wick above 1% in 2017Q2, M1 autocorrelation -0.36. This is pessimistic for stops and optimistic for any limit or mean-reversion rule, so I used none.
- Dukascopy's real spread was 116-181 bp on BTC and 122-444 bp on ETH in 2018-2020. Under that historical model both rules lose heavily (PF 0.24-0.42); the market was not tradable at those quotes then. The FP frames replace it with 2.2 bp (BTC) and 6.5 bp (ETH).
- A small stale-quote signature exists: +2 to +4 bp of continuation in the first minute after a signal. It is gone by 5 minutes and does not carry the result.
- Validation years 2022-2023 have 5-12% of minutes missing.

4. FP cost frame. The modelled spread is today's FP value scaled by each day's own intraday shape, so a weekend day has the same median spread as a weekday; real weekend crypto spreads at a retail broker are probably wider. The BTC 20 USD and ETH 2 USD spreads are provisional, and the BTC sleeve's validation pass disappears with about 2 bp of extra round-trip cost.

5. Swap. The engine charges five business nights plus a triple Wednesday and nothing at weekends; crypto CFDs are usually charged every day. The weekly total is the same, the distribution differs.

6. `r2.null_test` in mode "day" draws random days without preserving weekday / weekend or volatility state. Both rules sat at the 100th percentile, so this does not change the conclusion.

7. No web search was possible (the shared search budget was already used up). FP Markets' crypto trading hours, weekend quoting and spreads were not verified, and no literature was re-checked.

# Track `crypto` — BTCUSD / ETHUSD CFDs (round 2, PROTOCOL_V2)

## Verdict
- **One finalist passes the pre-registered criteria, weakly: `brk72_24h_wd`** — weekday 72-hour close-channel breakout on H1 bars, fixed 3 x ATR stop, 24-hour exit, on BTC and ETH.
- **One finalist fails validation: `sess_8_8_13_wd`** — Asia-session direction held from 08:00 to 21:00 UTC.
- The breakout's edge fell about 83% between in-sample and validation and is now roughly the size of its costs. BTC is positive only in R terms, 2025 was negative, and BTC cannot be sized prudently on a 1,000 EUR account. If anything is kept, I would keep ETH only, at small weight.
- Nothing on this track delivers several trades a day or fast growth: the surviving rule trades about 0.45 times a day per instrument.

## 1. Data check (structure only, before any rule)
| | BTCUSD | ETHUSD |
|---|---|---|
| First bar | 2017-05-07 | 2018-01-01 |
| Weekend quotes | none 2017-18; 95% / 89% of weekend days in 2019 / 2020; all from 2021 | none 2018; 70% / 84% in 2019 / 2020; all from 2021 |
| Minutes present | 66% (2017), 69% (2018), 93% (2019), 94% (2020), 99.5% (2021) | 66% (2018), 77% (2019), 88% (2020), 99.5% (2021) |
| Dukascopy real spread, median | 181 / 145 / 116 / 19 bp in 2018 / 19 / 20 / 21 | 213 / 444 / 122 / 20 bp |
| FP model spread | 2.18 bp (20 USD) | 6.48 bp (2 USD) |

- In-sample is 4.65 years for BTC and 4 years for ETH; only 2021 is clean 24/7 data.
- BTC quotes in May-September 2017 bounce by 1-2% within the minute (1,950 spike bars in 2017Q2, 410 in Q3). This penalises stops and would flatter limit or mean-reversion entries, so I used market entries only.
- Validation years 2022-2023 have 5-12% of minutes missing; 2024-25 are complete.

## 2. What was tested and why
**Descriptive pass on in-sample bars (no engine):** variance ratios, sign-momentum by horizon (15 cells per instrument), breakout follow-through (24 cells), session hand-offs (8 pairs).
- Hourly returns do not trend unconditionally (variance ratios 0.80-1.0 at 4-8 h).
- Momentum appears at 12-24 h and after new multi-day extremes; the first 4 h after a breakout add nothing.

finalists.name: noise30
finalists.rule: US100 CFD, New York wall-clock time, mid prices ((bid+ask)/2). Trade only on regular US cash sessions (Monday-Friday, not an NYSE holiday, not a 13:00 early-close day). (1) At 09:30: O = open of the 09:30 one-minute bar. PC = close of the 15:59 one-minute bar of the previous regular session (if that session was an early close, ignore PC and use O alone). (2) At each check time T = 10:00, 10:30, ..., 15:30 (12 checks): p = close of the one-minute bar that starts at T minus 1 minute (skip the check if the last quote is more than 10 minutes old). sigma(T) = average over the previous 14 regular sessions (at least 9 with data) of |p_d(T)/O_d - 1|. UB = max(O,PC)*(1+sigma(T)); LB = min(O,PC)*(1-sigma(T)). (3) State machine, state = flat/long/short, flat at the start of each day: (a) if state is long and p < UB, or state is short and p > LB: close any open position at market, state = flat; (b) if state is flat and p > UB: buy at market with stop-loss at max(O,PC), state = long; if flat and p < LB: sell at market with stop-loss at min(O,PC), state = short (when a and b fire at the same check the back-test opens the new position one minute later); (c) if the stop-loss is hit the state does not change, so no new entry is allowed until test (a) passes at a later check. (4) At 15:55 close any open position. (5) Size = chosen % of equity divided by the entry-to-stop distance, rounded down to 0.1 lot. No target, no other trailing. One position at a time, never held overnight.
finalists.notes: Published rule with the published parameters, no tuning. Judged alone on us100 (best of three indices: selection). IS criteria all met; random-entry null 100th percentile (rule +0.0775 R vs null max +0.030 R). Money value is in USD (0.1 lot, 1 unit per lot): median stop 120 points = 12.0 USD, 90th percentile 20.8 USD. CAVEATS: (1) execution: the data show a +0.4 to +0.5 bp continuation in the single minute after HH:00 / HH:30 when the price is outside the band; the back-test gets it by filling at the first tick of that minute. With the whole check grid shifted by +1/+2/+5/+15/+30 minutes the IS PF is 1.175/1.170/1.249/1.231/1.252 (t 2.1 to 2.9), so count on PF about 1.2 live, not 1.28. finalists.name: ocm4
finalists.rule: US100 CFD, New York wall-clock time, mid prices. Regular US cash sessions only (Monday-Friday, not an NYSE holiday, not a 13:00 early-close day). (1) At 09:34:00: O = open of the 09:30 one-minute bar; C = close of the 09:33 one-minute bar (at least 3 of the 4 bars 09:30-09:33 must exist). move = C/O - 1. (2) med = median of |move| over the previous 20 sessions (at least 10 with data). (3) If |move| >= med and move is not 0: buy at market if move > 0, sell at market if move < 0, on the first tick at or after 09:34:00. (4) Stop-loss at 0.3 x ATR14 from the fill price, where ATR14 = simple average of the true range of the last 14 completed daily bars (days ending 17:00 New York, days with fewer than 600 one-minute bars ignored), i.e. iATR(D1,14) of the previous day on an FP Markets server. No engine bug found; one fix in my own helper (empty ATR array on a frame shorter than one trading day), which does not change any result.

1. Fill timing is the main modelling limit. Market orders fill at the first tick of the minute plus 0.2 bp. The M1 data show a real clock effect: when the price is outside the noise band, the minute starting at HH:00 or HH:30 continues by +0.4 to +0.5 bp (t 5 to 6) and the minute 09:35-09:36 continues a large first 5-minute candle by +1.8 bp on us100 (t 6.5), +1.0 bp us500, +0.9 bp us30. At other minutes there is nothing, and the feed has no general one-minute autocorrelation (0.008), so it is not a smoothed feed. M1 bars cannot tell whether a retail order sent in the first second still gets that price. I recommend the lead run the one-minute-late stress on validation (noise30: first_min=601,last_min=931; ocm4: delay=1) and check tick data if available.

2. Cost frame: the cash-session spread in the FP frames is 0.7 times the headline because of the Dukascopy intraday shape (us100 0.42 bp, about 1.0 point, against 1.5 points headline; us500 0.55 bp; us30 0.30 bp). If FP's real cash-session spread is the full headline, the true cost is close to the x1.5 stress. Both finalists pass that stress in IS (PF 1.24 and 1.22) and in validation (1.19 and 1.27). The cost file is still marked provisional.

3. Data: a daily 15-minute hole at 19:15-19:30 UTC from January to early May 2014; the session ends at 16:00 New York in 2016-2017 and 16:15 in other years (exits at 15:55 are safe); data stop at 15:11 New York on 2015-11-02 to 05 and early on 2014-12-31 and 2015-12-31, where gl.exit_index exits on the last bar before the hole (6 IS days). Flat minutes are removed from the M1 frames, so everything is looked up by time with a 10-minute staleness limit.

4. The report t-statistic is per trade and ignores same-day clustering; for noise30 the day-clustered t is 3.18 against 3.12 per trade.

5. r2.evaluate appends a second line to trials.jsonl when a configuration is re-run at full depth: 94 lines for 87 distinct configurations.

## Verdict
Two sleeves, both on us100, pass the in-sample (IS, 2014-2021) and validation (VAL, 2022-2025) criteria. The edge is modest and depends partly on execution: expect a profit factor of about 1.2 and an annual Sharpe of about 1 per sleeve.

At 1% risk per trade that is a median of about +2% a month. The +50% a month target is out of reach on this track.

## The two rules
**noise30** is the noise-area rule of Zarattini, Aziz and Barbon (2024) with their parameters, untouched.
- At 10:00, 10:30, ..., 15:30 New York, compare the price with a band around the day's reference.
- The reference is max/min of the 09:30 open and the previous 16:00 price; the half-width is the average absolute move from the open to that time of day over the last 14 sessions.
- Outside the band: enter in that direction. Back inside at a later check, or at 15:55: exit. Hard stop at the band centre.
- In IS 91% of exits are the band exit or 15:55 and 9% the hard stop; the win rate is 38%, the average winner +0.93 R, the average loser -0.44 R, the median hold 60 minutes.

**ocm4** trades the direction of the first 4 minutes after the cash open, only when that move is at least the 20-session median.
- Market entry at 09:34, stop 0.3 x daily ATR(14), flat at 15:55, at most one trade a day.
- Half the trades end at the stop (-1 R); the rest average +1.3 R.

The exact, codable rules are in the `rule` field of each finalist and in the docstring of `strategy.py`.

## What was tested (87 configurations, all logged; 94 lines in trials.jsonl)
Before any engine trial I ran two descriptive studies on IS (mid prices, no costs, no stops, about 100 cells per index). These are soft trials and should be counted as such. They showed:
- End-of-day momentum is at or below cost: +1.4 / +0.6 / +0.4 bp gross per trade on us100 / us500 / us30.
- The gap carries no information (t between -1.7 and +1.1).
- The direction of the first 1 to 6 minutes predicts the rest of the day on us100 (+4.5 to +6.8 bp, t 2.2 to 3.3) and fades for longer candles.
- Only opening candles larger than the 20-session median carry that information (us100: +12 to +14 bp against about 0 for small candles).

## The execution finding that shaped the choice
The one-minute-late test exposed a clock effect in the data.
- When the price is outside the noise band, the single minute starting at HH:00 or HH:30 continues by +0.4 to +0.5 bp (t 5 to 6). At other minutes there is nothing.
- After a large first 5-minute candle, the minute 09:35-09:36 continues by +1.8 bp on us100 (t 6.5), +1.0 bp on us500 and +0.9 bp on us30. Candles of 1 to 4 minutes show no such burst.
- The feed has no general one-minute autocorrelation (0.008), so this is market behaviour at crowded clock times, not a smoothed feed.

The back-test captures these moves by filling at the first tick of the minute. Whether a retail order does is unknown from M1 data. Two consequences:
- **noise30** was kept on the published grid, but its realistic PF is about 1.2 (the range of the shifted grids, 1.17 to 1.25), not 1.28.
- **The opening rule was moved from 5 to 4 minutes.** The 5-minute version had the best IS numbers (PF 1.31) but loses them one minute late (1.17). The 4-minute version enters before the crowded minute and is unchanged one minute late.

I did not run a latency stress on validation, to respect the single shot; the parameters to do it are in `candidates.json`.

## Process
- The finalists were written to `finalists_preval.json` before any validation access; the validation log shows one `r2.validate` call per sleeve. Nothing was changed afterwards.
- Causality: orders rebuilt on frames cut at 66 minutes (26 around the decision minutes, 40 random) are identical to the full-frame orders (132 comparisons, 101,794 orders, 0 differences).
- An independent pandas recomputation of 8 trades matches bands, medians, ATR and stops.
- Orders built on a frame starting two months earlier are identical after the warm-up. For the 2026 holdout, load from 2025-10-01.

## Caveats to weigh
- **Selection.** us100 is the best of three indices; the same rules give PF 1.09 to 1.14 on us500 (t 1.2 to 1.6, edge about twice the cost) and at most 1.10 on us30.
- **Significance.** The validation t-statistics are 1.9 and 2.3; ocm4 passes the IS t bar narrowly (2.69) and several of its neighbours sit below 2.5.
- **Concentration.** The 10 best days give 53% (noise30) and 47% (ocm4) of the IS total. In validation, noise30 shorts earned nothing and 2025 gives 54% of ocm4's total.
- **Erosion.** ocm4's gross edge per trade halved between the two halves of IS, and its IS drawdown reached 37 R.
- **Same instrument.** Both sleeves trade us100 and are 0.32 correlated day by day.
- **Hourly checks.** The noise-area rule did better in-sample with hourly checks on both indices (us100 PF 1.36, us500 1.23). I did not adopt it; it is worth a look in the demo phase, not on validation.

research_gold2.engine_concerns:
1. numba on-disk cache breaks when one strategy file is imported under two module names. lab/holdout.py and lab/audit/audit.py import round-1 strategies as "strategy_<track>", the round-1 agents imported them as "strategy". Repro: import lab/tracks/trend/strategy.py under any other name and call make_orders with the finalist -> ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'strategy_trend' (raised while numba loads the cached overload). Workaround: set NUMBA_CACHE_DIR to a private folder. My own first port check (11:00 UTC) wrote three such cache files into lab/tracks/orb/__pycache__ and lab/tracks/pivots/__pycache__ (git-ignored, no source touched); I deleted those three .nbc files again (the .nbi index files still list them; numba treats a missing data file as a cache miss and recompiles). My strategy.py uses cache=False so it cannot be hit by this.
2. Round-1 rule rn100_break_fresh has a small look-ahead: it skips trading days with fewer than 600 M1 bars, which is only known at the end of the day. 23 of its 228 in-sample orders are triggered before 600 bars of the day exist; cutting the data 3 minutes after such a trigger removes the order (results/r2/gold2/engine_notes_checks.json). Effect on P&L is small, and the rule is not a candidate.
3. Fill-bar rule is pessimistic for stop entries: a stop-loss inside the fill bar is booked as hit even when the adverse extreme came before the fill (hand-checked example 2014-07-02 12:15 UTC). 18 of the finalist's 1030 in-sample trades (-18.5 R) are of this kind. Conservative, not a flaw.
4. r2.null_test is easy to pass for any breakout rule and does not detect duplication: every in-sample pass here scored the 100th percentile while most were spanned by the legacy sleeve. A spanning check against existing sleeves (weekly R regression: alpha t, share of trades inside legacy trades) would be a useful protocol addition; code in lab/r2/tracks/gold2/spanning.py and decomp.py.
5. Costs: fp_costs.json is marked provisional. The 1h breakout rules are cost-sensitive (finalist IS PF 1.25 -> 1.13 at x1.5 -> 1.04 at x2 -> 0.87 at x3; legacy sleeve 1.51 -> 1.46 -> 1.40 -> 1.30). With the real 2013-2021 Dukascopy spread (median 0.30 USD against 0.09 USD in the FP model) the finalist's IS PF is 1.115, and 1.006 with round-1 costs.
6. FP frame construction: the intraday spread shape divides by that trading day's median Dukascopy spread, a full-day statistic, so each minute's quotes carry a little end-of-day information. Harmless for these rules.
7. Time exits on closures: my port of the round-1 range breakouts exits on the last bar before a closure (gl.exit_index, as the README asks) where the round-1 code exited on the first bar after it; 52-87 of about 2000 orders differ by one bar, everything else is identical (results/r2/gold2/port_check.json).
8. Bracket live across the daily break: a bracket placed at the 17:00 New York close stays live during the reopen hour, where spreads are wide. For the finalist these entries (35 in-sample) are slightly negative, so they do not flatter the result; an EA should still avoid them.
9. No engine bug found. The legacy sleeve reproduces exactly under FP costs with my re-implementation (IS n 495, PF 1.512, t 3.17), and all round-1 ports build identical orders to the round-1 code.

# Events track (round 2): FOMC, NFP and CPI on xauusd, us100, us500

## 1. Verdict
**Nothing survives.** One rule passed every in-sample criterion and then failed the single-shot validation on both sleeves:

| EV_PREM_LONG | IS 2013-2021 us500 | IS us100 | VAL 2022-2025 us500 | VAL us100 |
|---|---|---|---|---|

| expectancy (R) | +0.0419 | +0.0407 | -0.0157 | -0.0170 |
| net bp per trade | +4.26 | +5.04 | -5.79 | -7.50 |

The other ideas in the brief (bracket before the release, momentum after it, pre-FOMC drift, CPI days) fail in sample. The gold follow-through after FOMC that round 1 flagged existed only in 2013-2017.

There is no event sleeve for the portfolio. Budget used: 78 logged trials of 120 (75 distinct symbol-and-parameter evaluations, 42 distinct parameter sets).

## 2. Method
- **Calendar** (`/home/user/gold-orb/lab/r2/tracks/events/calendars.py`): FOMC statement days at 14:00 New York, NFP and CPI at 08:30 New York, 2013 to 2027.
  - FOMC and NFP lists from round 1 were re-checked against federalreserve.gov and ALFRED release 50.
  - CPI dates come from the BLS archive, cross-checked against ALFRED release 10.
  - Dropped: 2013-01-30 FOMC (released at 14:15), unscheduled 2020 actions, and ALFRED's extra revision dates.
  - Irregular shutdown dates are kept (2013-10-22, 2013-10-30, 2025-10-24, 2025-11-20, 2025-12-16, 2025-12-18, 2026-02-11, 2026-02-13).
  - In sample: 70 FOMC, 108 NFP, 108 CPI = 286 releases.
- **Data**: FP cost frames, research period only. All descriptive work used frames cut at 2022-01-01. 2026 was never loaded.
- **Descriptive phase** (in sample, mid prices): about 740 heavily overlapping cells, so roughly 9 would show |t| >= 2.5 by chance. The pre-validation file says about 630; one table was under-counted there.
- **Engine phase**: one strategy module with five rule types (`long`, `short`, `mom`, `fade`, `brk`), every evaluation logged with `r2.log_trial`.
- **Causality**: truncation test passed for all six rule configurations on us500 and for the finalist on us500 and us100 (0 mismatches over 12 cuts, about 1,950 orders compared each). A frame starting 2021-09-01 reproduces the full-frame orders after the ATR warm-up.

## 3. What the in-sample data show (2013-2021, mid prices, bp)

**Average long path from T-5m, all releases pooled (t in brackets):**

| | T+5m | T+15m | T+30m | T+60m | 15:55 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| us500 | +4.4 (2.7) | +5.1 (2.9) | +5.2 (2.8) | +6.1 (2.6) | +9.0 (2.0) |
| us100 | +4.8 (2.6) | +5.9 (2.8) | +5.7 (2.7) | +7.5 (2.7) | +14.2 (2.6) |
| xauusd | +1.4 (0.5) | +3.7 (1.2) | +3.2 (1.0) | +4.3 (1.1) | +6.8 (1.3) |

- **The only pooled effect** was a positive average reaction of the indices to the release itself: FOMC +8 to +9 bp and NFP +6 bp by T+5m, CPI nil. Nothing before the release (T-4h to T-5m: -1.1 / -2.4 bp).
- **Release days against ordinary days**, 08:25 to 15:55: us500 +11.1 against +2.8 bp (difference t 1.5); us100 +15.7 against +2.4 (t 1.9); gold +5.9 against -2.8 (t 1.4).
- **Pre-FOMC 24-hour drift**: +6.2 bp (us500, t 1.0) and +7.2 bp (us100, t 0.9). The Lucca-Moench drift is not in this sample.
- **Continuation of the first move** (sign of the move at T+5m times the return to 15:55): us500 -5.8 (t -1.3), us100 -3.4 (t -0.6), gold +1.4 (t 0.3). The exception is gold after FOMC: +21.5 bp to 15:55 (t 2.8) and +41.6 bp to the next close (t 2.2), n = 70.
- **Bracket logic** (price outside the 30-minute pre-release range at T+5m, held to 15:55): -3.3, -0.9, +1.2 bp, all |t| < 0.7.
- **CPI** was a small event in sample: the release minute moved us500 by 8 bp against 21-23 bp for FOMC and NFP, and gold by 20 bp against 39-47 bp.

## 5. Finalist EV_PREM_LONG
**Rule**: on US500 and US100, buy at market 5 minutes before every FOMC statement, NFP and CPI release; stop 1.0 x ATR_D(14) below the fill; close 15 minutes after the release. Parameters: `{"rule":"long","kinds":"fomc+nfp+cpi","lead":5,"exit":"hold","hold":15,"stop_atr":1.0,"atr_n":14}`.

It was fixed in `/home/user/gold-orb/lab/results/r2/events/finalists_preval.json` at 11:13:09 UTC with zero prior validation accesses by this track; the first access is logged at 11:14:14.

### In sample

| n >= 250 | 268 (31.4 a year) | 267 (31.4 a year) |

| random-entry null >= 97.5 | 100 ('time' and 'day') | 100 ('time' and 'day') |
| **all pass** | yes | yes |

Other in-sample numbers (us500 / us100):
- Win rate 56.7% / 60.3%; max drawdown 2.8 R / 2.3 R; average hold 0.3 h.
- Net +4.26 / +5.04 bp per trade; gross +5.40 / +6.02 bp; gross PF 1.82 / 1.80.
- Long only: +11.2 R / +10.9 R, no short side.
- Gross edge by half: +4.81 then +5.93 bp (us500); +5.07 then +6.86 bp (us100). No erosion inside the sample.
- By kind, net: FOMC +8.9 / +11.5 bp (t 2.1 / 2.4); NFP +5.6 / +5.2 (t 1.9); CPI -0.2 / +0.6 (t 0.1).
- Median stop distance in 2024-2025: 66.2 points on US500 (6.6 USD on the 0.1 minimum lot) and 311 points on US100 (31 USD, at the limit for a 1,000 EUR account).

**Weaknesses written down before validation:**
- us500 and us100 are one bet: R correlation 0.94, event-clustered basket t 2.70 against a naive 3.82.
- The edge came from FOMC and NFP only.
- t without the 5 best trades: 1.78 / 1.91.
- It was found after hundreds of descriptive cells and a grid of 8, so the in-sample t is biased upward.
- Costs x3: PF 1.24 / 1.36. Under the historical Dukascopy spread: PF 1.39 / 1.28, t 1.84 / 1.38.
- The stop is a disaster stop (hit once in 268 trades on us500, never on us100), so R is compressed: standard deviation 0.26 / 0.24 R.

### Validation 2022-2025 (one shot per sleeve, nothing re-tuned)
Both sleeves fail all three criteria (PF >= 1.06, expectancy > 0, every-signal expectancy > 0); headline numbers are in section 1.

| | us500 | us100 |
|---|---|---|
| R by year 2022 / 2023 / 2024 / 2025 | -5.0 / +2.0 / -0.9 / +1.9 | -5.0 / +1.9 / -0.9 / +2.0 |
| FOMC, net bp per trade (winners) | -15.7 (38%) | -18.3 (41%) |
| NFP, net bp per trade | -4.0 | -8.9 |
| CPI, net bp per trade | -0.9 | +1.3 |
| stops hit | 7 of 126 | 5 of 126 |
| R standard deviation | 0.44 | 0.41 |

- Basket: pooled PF 0.90, event-clustered t -0.43.
- It loses before costs (about -4.6 / -6.5 bp gross), so no cost revision rescues it.
- Over 2013-2025 together the us500 t is about 1.4.

**Reading**: the positive reaction of 2013-2021 did not persist. The FOMC statement window went from +10 bp to -16 bp per event, and 2022 alone cost 5 R. 2023-2025 taken alone is mildly positive (+0.03 R per trade), but that is a post-hoc slice and changes nothing.

## 6. Not a finalist: gold momentum after FOMC
Five minutes after the statement, follow the first move; stop 0.5 ATR_D; exit next day 15:55.
- In sample: n 70, PF 2.31, t 2.57, +45.7 bp per trade, stress PF 2.28, null 100th percentile, neighbour PFs 1.64-2.55.
- It fails n >= 250 by construction (8 events a year), and no basket exists because the indices show no continuation (PF 1.03 / 1.18).
- The edge is entirely in the first half: +103.9 bp per trade gross (t 4.0) in 2013 to mid-2017, -6.1 bp (t -0.35) from mid-2017 to 2021. R by year: +14.0, +10.4, +17.1, +1.6, +11.9, then -6.7, +0.4, -5.5, +3.4. Every exit variant shows the same break.
- I chose not to spend a validation access on it. Round 1's "t about 2.3" was a 2013-2017 phenomenon.

## 7. Engine and data concerns
1. `r2.null_test` is not discriminating for event-window rules: random windows are much calmer, so the finalist scored 100th percentile with a t of 2.65 and still failed validation.
2. Pooled basket t-statistics ignore cross-instrument correlation (3.82 naive against 2.70 clustered here). This matters for any us100 / us500 / us30 basket in other tracks.
3. The FP frames carry almost no news widening on the indices (0.74 bp at the close of the release minute, the same as 30 minutes earlier). Rules that enter or get stopped in the release minute are flattered.
4. The forward-looking index spread is 3 to 4 times tighter than the historical Dukascopy spread at 08:25 New York. Whether FP's 0.5 / 1.5 point spreads hold before the 09:30 open should be checked.
5. `fp_costs.json` is still provisional; the verdict does not depend on it.
6. Data holes: the indices have no usable quotes around 08:30 New York from January to May 2013 and too few full days for a daily ATR until June 2013 (18 of 286 in-sample releases not traded); four Good Friday releases have no market.

## 8. What this means for the robot
- Do not build an entry rule on FOMC, NFP or CPI: before, during or after the release, nothing holds out of sample.
- Untested suggestion for the portfolio simulation: use the calendar as a risk filter. The release minute moves the indices 21-23 bp and gold 39-47 bp in one bar, and real spreads there are worse than the model, so tight-stop sleeves held through 08:30 or 14:00 New York on these days deserve a check.
- Not tested: other releases (ISM, PPI, retail sales, GDP), which were outside the brief's calendar and would have had low power in sample, and btcusd (too few releases).

finalists.name: nq_btc_follow
finalists.rule: Sleeve on BTCUSD, signal from US100 (Nasdaq-100 CFD); everything on M1 bars labelled by start time, mid prices ((bid+ask)/2) of bar closes. At the close of every US100 M1 bar whose START is between 09:30 and 15:59 New-York local time (Mon-Fri; New-York clock with US daylight saving, not broker server time): r = ln(C0/C1), C0 = close of that bar, C1 = close of the bar one minute earlier (if that minute has no bar, the last close within the 3 previous minutes, else no signal). sigma_us100 = sqrt(mean(r_i^2)) over all US100 M1 bars of the previous 20 calendar days (28,800 minutes ending one minute before the current bar; r_i = the same 1-minute log return, only minutes that have a bar; at least 4,800 values, else no signal). If |r| >= 6 * sigma_us100, BTCUSD also printed a bar in that minute, and this sleeve has no open position: send a MARKET order on BTCUSD at the first tick of the next minute, BUY if r > 0, SELL if r < 0. Stop-loss at distance D = 2 * sigma_btc * sqrt(60) * (last BTCUSD M1 close) from the fill, where sigma_btc = RMS of BTCUSD 1-minute log returns over the previous 20 calendar days (same definition; D is about 1.2-1.5 % of price). No take-profit, no trailing, no break-even. Close at market at the first tick 60 minutes after the entry bar's open time. One position at a time: signals occurring while a position is open are ignored (no re-entry queue). Lot size = floor(risk money / (D * contract size) / lot step) * lot step.

1. Crypto frames. Dukascopy's real BTC spread was 3.9 bp (2017), 181, 145, 116, 19 bp (2018-2021), 35, 25, 11, 5 bp (2022-2025); ETH 213, 444, 122, 20 bp (2018-2021). The FP frame keeps that mid and replaces the spread by 2.18 bp (BTC) / 6.48 bp (ETH). The mid of such a wide quote lags the real market, so any rule entering within 1-2 minutes of a crypto move looks excellent and is not real (my 'ether burst -> bitcoin' rule: PF 1.5-1.9, t 5-7, gone with a 1-2 minute delay). In addition the spread 'shape' contains no burst widening for crypto (modelled cost at the 0.1 % tail = median cost). Recommendation: for every crypto sleeve of any track require an entry-delay probe (1, 2, 5 minutes), distrust holds under about 15 minutes, and replicate the signal on FP Markets' own M1 history exported from MT5 before any demo.
2. The same reservation applies, more mildly, to my finalist: in-sample it was not capturable on Dukascopy in 2018-2020 (historical-spread run: PF 0.10); the forward-looking model assumes FP's tight quote shows the same 60-minute drift.
3. Index CFD history has only 02:00-16:00 New-York hours from mid-2015 to 2017 and is partial in 2013 (no evening / Asian session then); US30 and GER40 start on 2013-09-30.
4. r2.is_criteria counts stub years as full years (BTC 2017 = 7 months, 97 trades): the finalist's 3/5 positive years depends on it.
5. r2.null_test mode 'day' draws random calendar days including weekends for 24/7 crypto, while a US-hours rule never trades weekends (minor).
6. gl.exit_index can postpone a time exit by up to 30 minutes over a data hole (finalist max hold 1.4 h in-sample for a 1.0 h plan) (minor).
7. Two-legged trades cannot be credited by per-sleeve statistics: the legs' market noise cancels in the pair but not inside a sleeve, so a hedged pair with pair-level t about 3 shows per-leg t about 1. A limitation of the frozen criteria, not a bug.
8. Cross-asset strategies need leader data that make_orders(m1) does not receive: strategy.set_leader(sym, frame) must be called before the holdout run, with >= 25 days of warm-up for both frames.

# Track `ml` — a learned filter on hourly breakouts ("our own indicator")

## Verdict

The learned filter works on one asset class only: **bitcoin and ether**. Both finalists pass every in-sample criterion and the single validation run, on both markets. I propose the filtered one.

- **F1, breakout + learned filter (proposed).** Validation 2022–2025: btcusd PF 1.33, 523 trades, +0.128 R per trade, 4/4 years; ethusd PF 1.22, 547 trades, +0.090 R per trade, 4/4 years.
- **F2, the same breakout without the filter (the baseline).** Validation: PF 1.14 on both markets, +0.053 and +0.054 R per trade. It passes, but its net edge is 2–3 bp per trade, about the size of its costs.
- **us100, ger40, xauusd: nothing survives.** The unfiltered breakout is break-even there and no model finds anything to learn (walk-forward PF 0.91–1.09, t below 1).

(R = result of a trade divided by the money risked to the stop. PF = gains / losses.)

Three warnings:

1. **The edge is shrinking.** btcusd went from +0.31 R per trade in-sample to +0.13 in validation; 2021 and 2025 were barely positive (+0.03 R per trade in 2021; +6.8 R for the whole of 2025).
2. **This is not "many small gains".** Half the trades lose a little; the top 5 % of trades bring about 92 % of the in-sample profit.
3. **It is slow and it is one bet.** About one trade per weekday for the two markets together, and their same-day results are 0.69 correlated. At 1 % risk per trade, the validation result is roughly +29 % a year for both sleeves together, nowhere near +50 % a month.

Trials: 85 logged (81 distinct configurations + 4 full re-evaluations), budget 120. Validation: one `r2.validate` call per finalist sleeve (4 calls, 12 log lines). Nothing was re-tuned.

## 1. What was built

**Candidate generator** (fixed before the first trial, identical on every market):

- H1 bars from bid prices. Only "session bars" are used: bars opening 02:00–15:00 New York, Monday–Friday (14 a day). Every look-back counts session bars only.
- Volatility unit A = average (high − low) of the last 70 session bars.
- At each hourly close from 03:00 to 15:00 New York: close above the highest high of the previous 14 session bars → long candidate; below the lowest low → short candidate.
- Market entry on the next minute, fixed stop, exit the same day. Nothing is held overnight, so there is no swap.

Why session bars only: the index data has no overnight quotes from March 2015 to March 2018 (and 2013 is half empty before 09:00 New York). 02:00–16:00 New York is the only window present in every year, so the same information is used throughout.

**Filter.** 13 scale-free inputs (distances divided by A and signed by the trade side) plus 3 time-of-day and 2 weekday dummies: breakout distance, size and body of the breakout bar, 4 / 14 / 70-bar returns, channel width, volatility ratio (5 sessions vs 20), position in the 20-session range, number of same-side and opposite breakouts in the last 14 bars, distance beyond the previous day's high or low, move since the previous close. Left out on purpose: trade side (it would learn "the market went up"), spread level, round numbers, result of the previous candidate.

**Training.** The label is the net R of every candidate taken on its own (engine, FP costs). One model is trained on the pooled candidates of us100 + ger40 + xauusd + btcusd, with one threshold for all markets. Walk-forward: for each year Y from 2016 to 2021, train on candidates decided before 1 January Y minus 5 days (maximum hold is 13 hours), predict year Y. Scaling and threshold come from the training fold only. All in-sample numbers of a filtered sleeve are these out-of-fold predictions, run through `r2.evaluate`.

The plan, including the model recipe and the threshold, was written to `plan_predeclared.txt` before the first trial.

## 2. Trials (85 logged)

| E | 2 | ethusd, baseline and filter (ethusd is never in the training pool) |

## 9. Caveats, data and engine concerns

- **Selection.** Crypto is one of four asset groups tried (six markets touched). The baseline effect is strong on its own (btcusd t 3.5, null 100th percentile), and the first pre-declared recipe was kept, so there was no selection among models.
- **Overlap with the crypto track.** F1 and F2 are almost certainly the same underlying effect as any bitcoin / ether breakout sleeve from the `crypto` track. Count them as one bet in the portfolio.
- **Short history.** btcusd in-sample is 2017-05 to 2021, ethusd 2018 to 2021. The "years positive" criterion rests on 4–5 years.
- **Early bitcoin data is thin.** 2017–2018 have 92 missing days and many short days (the `crypto` track's data check). `gl.exit_index` moves a time exit to the last bar before a data hole longer than 30 minutes, which an EA cannot know; it is not directional but it touches 2017–2018 results.
- **Costs are provisional** (`fp_costs.json`): constant 2.2 bp on btcusd and 6.5 bp on ethusd at all hours. FP Markets' real crypto spread, trading hours and 1:20 leverage could not be verified: the shared web-search budget was exhausted, so no source was consulted in this session.
- **Server clock.** The rule assumes FP server time = New York + 7 hours all year. Check it at install; otherwise compute New-York time in the EA.
- **`r2.null_test`** draws random days from all calendar days, week-ends included, while the rule trades Monday–Friday. The rule is still at the 100th percentile, and the random-side null at its own entry times agrees.
- **No basket helper in the toolkit.** I pooled the in-sample trades myself; my replica of the null reproduces `r2.null_test` exactly on each sleeve (100 / 100 / 100 / 99.5).
- **No engine bug found.** One behaviour to know: with one position at a time, an order activating on the bar where the previous trade exits is skipped.
- **Warm-up for the 2026 holdout.** Load M1 from 2025-11-01 and keep trades entered from 2026-01-01 (a frame starting 6 weeks earlier gives identical orders).

findings.claim: Entity: 1:500 is offered by several non-EU FP Markets entities, and public sources cannot tell which one holds a given account. www.fpmarkets.com (global site and the EU-language regional pages such as /en-de/ and /en-fr/) is operated by FP Markets Ltd, Saint Lucia, registration 2025-00853, which is a company registration and not a financial licence. The /en-sc/ site is operated by First Prudential Markets Limited, Seychelles FSA licence SD130, whose Client Agreement says 'The Company offers leverage up to 1:500'. FP Markets (Pty) Ltd (South Africa, FSCA FSP 50926) is also listed at 1:500 by FXEmpire. Both offshore sites say they do not offer services to EEA residents, yet the EU-language pages show a pop-up asking visitors to confirm they came on their 'own exclusive initiative'; the Saint Lucia Client Agreement excludes only the US, Australia, Japan, North Korea, Iran, Iraq and Belgium and contains a clause for French residents. The user must read the entity from the account-opening documents or the MT5 server name.

The former St Vincent entity FP Markets LLC (126 LLC 2019) was rebranded FP Trading LLC effective 28 March 2026 and now runs fptrading.com, with FP Trading Ltd (Saint Lucia 2026-00106), FP Trading (MU) Limited (Mauritius FSC GB26205878) and FPK Trading (Pty) (FSCA 52858). Clients onboarded under FP Markets LLC were moved to that brand and a renamed MetaTrader server. The rebrand date comes from a client notice quoted by two third-party sites, not from an official page I could read. fptrading.com publishes the same swap table as FP Markets and a spread table labelled May 2026 with identical FX figures and gold at 0.22.

FP Markets' own spread table, labelled November 2026 and identical on the Saint Lucia and Seychelles sites, gives Standard account averages of EURUSD 1.26 pips, GBPUSD 1.56 pips, USDJPY 1.61 pips, XAUUSD 0.24 USD and XAGUSD 0.04 USD. Raw minimum/average are EURUSD 0/0.16, GBPUSD 0/0.46, USDJPY 0.1/0.52, XAUUSD 0.05/0.10 and XAGUSD 0.02/0.03. Only averages are published for Standard, with no method or time window stated.

RinTrade: 0.23 average, range 0.22-0.23, live MT5 Standard on server FPMarketsSC-Live, 9 Jul 2026, 10:00-19:00 UTC, 511 one-minute samples. All were taken in London/New York hours; none covers the Asian session, the daily break or news.

Standard versus Raw on gold: Raw is published at 0.10 average plus 3 USD per side commission (6 USD round trip per lot, or 2.75 EUR per side on EUR accounts), which adds 0.06 USD per oz, so about 0.16 all-in. Measured Raw spreads were 0.15 (FXEmpire, 28 Apr 2026), 0.12 (FXEmpire, 19 Oct 2026), 0.14 with an NFP peak of 0.55 (lowspreadbroker, 10-24 Mar 2026), 0.13 (BrokersProfile) and 0.09 average / 0.06 minimum (BestBrokers), giving 0.15-0.21 all-in. The holiday page (times in GMT+3) shows XAUUSD and XAGUSD 'Close @20:30' on two late-November dates and warns that spreads may be significantly wider in holiday periods.

Contract sizes and lots: minimum trade size 0.01 lot on Standard and Raw. The MetaTrader PDS (29 Mar 2021, ASIC entity) states 'minimum contract size is 0.01 Lot (step 0.01 Lot) with 1 Lot of gold being equivalent to 100 ounces and 1 lot of silver being equivalent to 5000 ounces', and FX 1 lot = 100,000 units of base currency. The current metals page confirms '100 oz of XAU/USD (1 lot of XAU/USD)' and the FAQ swap example uses 100,000 for EURUSD. Maximum is 50 lots per trade on Forex. The 5,000 oz silver size is not restated on current offshore pages.

Automated trading: the marketing pages and the Client Agreement disagree. The FAQ says EAs, scalping and hedging are allowed, with a cap of 5,000 account 'movements' per 24 hours on the Saint Lucia site (10,000 on the Seychelles site). Both Client Agreements (updated 22 June 2026), clause 14.14, say use of 'robots, spiders or other automated data entry system' is 'expressly prohibited, unless you receive express written consent', and list scalping and robots under 'Abusive Trading', which lets the broker nullify profits. Scalping is defined there as opening too many positions at once and closing them in under five minutes. For an automated intraday strategy, written confirmation from support that the EA is permitted is worth obtaining.

Stops level and execution: the FAQ on both offshore sites says 'We do not place a minimum level for your stop loss/take profit or pending orders', while Client Agreement App. A 2.10 says SL/TP can be changed 'as long as they are higher in distance than a specific level (depending on the trading symbol)'. Stop loss, take profit, limit and stop orders are executed at the first available market price, so slippage applies and is not guaranteed symmetric (positive slippage 'can' be passed on). Under force majeure the broker may increase spreads, decrease leverage and change the stop-out level without notice. One third-party test on a Raw MT5 account (ASIC entity, Feb-Mar 2026, 480 market orders) reported zero requotes and slippage on 13.6% of gold orders, split about evenly positive and negative.

Margin rules on the offshore entities: margin call at 100% margin level and stop-out at 20%, per the FAQ and the metals page example (FXEmpire reports 50% for the ASIC entity). Negative balance protection is stated in the FAQ and in Client Agreement clause 18.3. The FAQ says there is no minimum deposit; FP Trading states 100 USD.

Leverage on gold is unresolved. Official material shows 1:500: the metals page example ('margin rate is 0.2% (Account leverage: 1:500)'), the FAQ ('1:1 up to 1:500, depending on your preference and the instrument') and FP Trading's table ('Metals 1:500'). FXEmpire's October 2026 test of the Saint Lucia entity reports 'Maximum Gold Leverage: 1:200', and BrokersProfile and CrowInvesting cite 1:100 for offshore metals. No dynamic or tiered leverage scheme was found. At 0.01-0.05 lots on a 1,000 EUR account the difference is small (about 8 to 41 USD margin per 0.01 lot of gold).

Myfxbook, ForexBenchmark and BrokerChooser gave nothing usable. Myfxbook's FP Markets pages returned 403; a search-index snapshot of the XAUUSD page showed 'Current Spread 9.0 pips' of unknown age, which matches Raw pricing (0.09 USD), not Standard. BestBrokers' cTrader figure of 9 pips reported by FX News Group (5 Oct 2026) is also a Raw-type figure. No FP Markets data was found on ForexBenchmark. BrokerChooser's '0.07' for XAU/USD could not be read (403) and its account type is unknown. No FP Markets-specific gold slippage complaints were found on Trustpilot or Forex Peace Army.

fp_sweeps.caveats:
1. Source access: www.fpmarkets.com returned HTTP 403 to the fetch tool and I did not try to get around its bot check. The official figures were read on 10 Nov 2026 from www.firstprudentialmarkets.com, which carries the same pages, footers (FP Markets Ltd Saint Lucia on the root, First Prudential Markets Limited Seychelles on /en-sc/), legal PDFs and a 2026 copyright. Its spread table matches what the search index shows for fpmarkets.com/forex-spreads/. I could not independently prove that this domain is operated by the broker, so confirm on fpmarkets.com in a browser.
2. The broker's spread table is a self-reported 'typical' average with no stated method or time window. The FX figures (1.26 / 1.56 / 1.61) are identical on FP Trading's table labelled May 2026, so they may be static. No Standard-account minimum spreads are published; the spread_min values are the lowest readings in one third-party sample, and USDJPY has none.
3. Every independent measurement was taken during London/New York hours on one or a few days. I found no measured FP Markets Standard data for the Asian session, the minutes around the gold break (23:59-01:00 server), the weekly open or news releases. The only widening figure is a Raw-account NFP peak of 0.55 USD from a low-authority site. A backtest should not assume 0.24 USD at all hours.
4. These must be read from the MT5 Symbol Specification on the user's own account before going live: exact symbol name and suffix, digits, contract size (silver's 5,000 oz comes from a 2021 ASIC-entity PDS), stops and freeze level, margin rate on gold and silver, the 3-day swap day and the session table. The USD and JPY swap amounts for silver and USDJPY are my conversions from points.
5. Swap rates are republished daily; the values given are for the 10 Nov 2026 rollover only.
6. Entity is not determinable from public sources. The offshore sites formally exclude EEA residents while running EU-language pages with an 'own initiative' pop-up. An EU retail client at 1:500 would most plausibly be under FP Markets Ltd (Saint Lucia, unlicensed registration) or First Prudential Markets Limited (Seychelles FSA), or under FP Trading if onboarded with FP Markets LLC before 28 March 2026. Protections differ from the CySEC entity.
7. The Client Agreements' prohibition on robots without written consent conflicts with the FAQ. I report both texts and cannot say how the broker enforces it.
8. Third-party sites (RinTrade, BestBrokers, FXEmpire, CompareForexBrokers, lowspreadbroker, BrokersProfile, InvestinGoal, DayTrading.com, CrowInvesting, topfxbrokersreview) are affiliate-funded, some with internal inconsistencies or unstated methods. I weighted those that name account type, platform, server and date. Myfxbook, BrokerChooser, Forex Peace Army and TradersUnion were blocked (403).
9. The Saint Lucia Client Agreement's leverage clause (App. A 7.1, 'by default, leverage of 1:30 to the Major Currencies') looks like boilerplate that contradicts the site's 1:500; the Seychelles agreement says 'up to 1:500'.
10. fp_sweeps.caveats:
1) The minimum lot and lot step for the four indices are NOT verified, and this is the number that decides which indices fit a EUR 1,000 account. FP's last own statements (2019 and 2021 PDS, an education guide of about 2023) say 1.00 lot minimum with a 1.00 step; two 2026 third-party reviews say 0.01; nothing supports 0.1. At 1.00 lot (USD or EUR 1 per point) only US500 is comfortably sized for this account. The user can settle it in seconds in MT5: right-click the symbol, Specification, Volume min and Volume step. Until then, plan on 1.00 as the conservative case.
2) Access limits. fpmarkets.com returns a Cloudflare 403 to automated fetches, so global-site content was read only through search-engine extracts, some of them from old cached page versions. First-hand readings come from the group's EU site (fpmarkets.eu, CySEC entity) and the sister-brand site fptrading.com (the former FP Markets LLC), which publish the same spread and swap tables. Several review sites (BrokerChooser, FXStreet, Myfxbook, TradersUnion, ForexPeaceArmy) also refused direct fetches and are quoted from search extracts. fpmarkets.international could not be resolved; it would have to be allowed in the session's network settings.
3) Entity uncertainty. From outside it cannot be determined whether the user's 1:500 account sits with First Prudential Markets Limited (Seychelles FSA) or with FP Trading LLC (the renamed St Vincent entity). The MT5 server name and the client agreement decide it. Index leverage of 1:200, the stop-out level, negative balance protection and the scalping clauses were confirmed only for FP Trading LLC or the EU entity, not from the Seychelles entity's own documents.
4) Spreads. The published figures are FP's 'typical' averages from a table that does not change month to month. They agree with the two most credible dated independent checks (FXEmpire on MT5 in April 2026, BestBrokers on cTrader in October 2026), but FP gives no time-of-day breakdown and no tick data was available. The only session-specific numbers come from low-reliability sites and are two to three times higher in US hours and more outside them. The project's provisional index spreads (US100 1.5, US500 0.5, US30 2.0, GER40 1.5) are about double FP's published typical for the US indices and close to that pessimistic set, so they work as a stress case rather than a base case. A week of logged spreads from the user's own MT5 would close this gap.
5) Not found, left null: stops level and freeze level, maximum lot, exact margin mode in MT5 (fixed percentage or tied to account leverage), FP's currency-conversion markup on USD profit and loss for a EUR account, and a per-index dividend schedule. GER40 hours conflict between FP's own pages (01:00-24:00 against 02:15-22:59 server time).
6) Swap values change daily and scale with the index level; the figures are those applied on 10 Nov 2026. Annualised percentages are my arithmetic on index levels of 6 Nov 2026, and the Nasdaq-100 level used (about 27,000) rests on a single unverified source.
7) Third-party review sites differ widely in reliability; several show internal errors (wrong entity names, inconsistent dates). I ranked FP's own documents first, then FXEmpire, RinTrade and BestBrokers (dated, method stated), and treated the rest as indicative only.

findings.claim: ENTITY FOR 1:500 (main one): the FP Markets global site, including at least its France pages (en-fr, fr-fr), is operated by FP Markets Ltd, a Saint Lucia company with registration number 2025-00853. This is a company registration only: no regulator or licence is named for it. Sign-ups go to the client-portal path 'stl-EN'. Its account-type table gives max leverage 1:500 for both Standard and Raw on MT4/MT5/cTrader, min trade size 0.01 lot, Standard spreads 'from 1.0 pips' with zero commission. Pages read 2026-11-10; the Saint Lucia client agreement was last modified 22 June 2026.

ENTITY FOR 1:500 (second one): First Prudential Markets Limited, Seychelles (registration 8426368-1, FSA licence SD130) operates the 'en-sc' site (portal path 'sc-EN'). Its client agreement (Last Update 22 June 2026), Appendix A 7.1, says 'The Company offers leverage up to 1:500.' Which of the two entities a client gets depends on residence and onboarding path: CompareForexBrokers describes the Seychelles company as the one for 'global clients' (US$100 minimum), and a Trustpilot review dated 27 Oct 2026 mentions an account being moved to the Seychelles entity. The contracting entity is shown in the application and account e-mail and should be checked.

WHO IS (NOT) ACCEPTED: the Saint Lucia site states it does not offer services to residents of the United States and the European Economic Area (among others), shows a gate where the visitor confirms acting 'at your own exclusive initiative' with no solicitation, and says its operator is not regulated by a UK or EU authority. The Seychelles site adds the United Kingdom and says it 'is not intended for residents of the European Union'. The Saint Lucia client agreement (2.1) refuses citizens/residents of the USA, Australia, Japan, North Korea, Iran, Iraq and Belgium. EEA residents are directed to First Prudential Markets Ltd (Cyprus, HE 372179, CySEC 371/18, fpmarkets.eu) where retail leverage is 1:30; the ASIC entity is also 1:30. So an EU-resident retail client only gets 1:500 through the offshore entity on an own-initiative basis (no EU investor compensation, no MiFID protections) or as a professional client of the CySEC entity (third-party table: Pro forex 1:500).

OTHER ENTITIES: First Prudential Markets Pty Ltd (ASIC AFSL 286354), FP Markets (Pty) Ltd (South Africa FSCA FSP 50926) and a Kenyan entity (CMA licence 193) are listed on the group page. The St Vincent company 'FP Markets LLC' (126 LLC 2019) was still named as a group company in the Seychelles agreement of 14 Oct 2024 but was replaced by the Saint Lucia company in the June 2026 agreements; FXEmpire's review of the separate 'FP Trading' brand (Oct 2026) lists 'FP Trading LLC' under that same SVG number. A Mauritius FSC entity (GB21026264) is cited by DayTrading.com and CompareForexBrokers but does not appear in the current global-site footer or group page.

MARGIN CALL / STOP-OUT (1:500 entities): the official FAQ on the Saint Lucia site (same wording on the Seychelles and French-language pages) says 'When your margin level falls to 100% you will be in margin call, and we will attempt to contact you via email' and 'Stop out is at 20% margin level, and trades will be automatically closed starting from those with the largest loss.' The metals and indices product pages repeat a close-out when free equity reaches 20% of initial margin. CONFLICT: FP Markets' own education guide says the stop-out level 'is set to 50% for FP Markets', the ASIC-entity FAQ gives 50%, and FXEmpire (updated 12 Oct 2026) lists margin call 100% / stop-out 50% for Standard and Raw. Contractually the broker has no obligation to issue a margin call and may close any or all positions without notice once margin requirements are not met (client agreement 15.1, 17.5, 17.6). 20% is the figure published for the 1:500 entities, but the real values should be read from the account (MT5 ACCOUNT_MARGIN_SO_CALL / ACCOUNT_MARGIN_SO_SO).

NEGATIVE BALANCE PROTECTION: FAQ: 'Yes, we offer Negative Balance Protection.' Both the Saint Lucia and Seychelles client agreements (clause 18.3) state 'The client is protected by the Company against negative account balances'. It is a contractual promise, not a regulatory guarantee, and 'negative balance protection abuse and/or possibility of abuse' is listed under 'Abusive Trading' (clause 1.1). Third-party reviews disagree (FXEmpire: 'Yes' for every entity; DayTrading.com: none for the offshore entities), and a Trustpilot review dated 7 Sep 2026 describes a disputed negative-balance reset followed by suspension for 'risky trading'.

DYNAMIC LEVERAGE: no published tier table (by equity, position size, news or weekend) was found on the leverage page, FAQ, account-type page, holiday-hours page or in the agreements. The leverage page only says leverage 'varies depending on the financial instrument, position size, and account type', with no thresholds. What the contract allows: leverage may be amended 'at any time at our absolute discretion' (Appendix A 7.4 Saint Lucia / 7.2 Seychelles); margin requirements may change with 5 business days' written notice for new positions, or without notice and on open positions in a force-majeure event, which includes 'an excessive movement' in a market (16.1(g), 17.3); in such events the broker may also increase spreads, decrease leverage and change the stop-out level (16.2); it may limit the number and size of open transactions based on account funds (17.1). The holiday-hours page only warns that spreads 'may be significantly wider during holiday periods'. A dated third-party review (Coin Bureau, 29 Mar 2023) mentions equity-based caps (up to 500:1 with max equity US$10,000; 100:1 at US$100k): unverified today and in any case not binding for a EUR 1,000 account.

SETTING LEVERAGE: account leverage is client-selected. FAQ: 'We offer leverage from 1:1 up to 1:500, depending on your preference and the instrument you are trading'; it is changed in the client portal ('Change Account Leverage' tab). The Saint Lucia agreement (Appendix A 7.1) says the company 'offers by default, leverage of 1:30 to the Major Currencies' unless other levels are made available on the platform and website, so the account should be checked to be actually set to 1:500. Official pages show metals at 'margin rate is 0.2% (Account leverage: 1:500)' and index CFDs at margins 'starting at just 1%' (a US30 worked example uses 0.5%).

SERVER TIME: FAQ: 'The server time on the platform is either GMT + 2 or GMT + 3 depending on Daylight savings. This ensures the daily candles can follow the NY close times'; swap is charged 'at 00:00 (Server time) - 5:00 PM New York time'; the trading-hours page says 'times displayed are GMT +2 or GMT +3 when DST takes effect'. Because server midnight is pegged to 17:00 New York, the switch follows US daylight saving (in 2026: GMT+3 from 8 March to 1 November, so GMT+2 on 2026-11-10; this is my calendar inference from the New York peg). In the weeks when US and European clock changes differ, London-session times move by one hour in server time. Forex and metals positions held over Wednesday night are charged triple swap.

SERVER NAMES AND LOCATION: the MT5 live server name is not published on the public pages read; FP Markets' guides say server details arrive in the registration e-mail. The FAQ names MT4 servers 'FPMarkets-live' (Raw symbols carry the suffix '.r') and 'FPMarkets-live2'; WikiFX shows 'FPMarkets-Demo2' (location United Kingdom) and counts 16 MT4 and 18 MT5 servers. Data centres: the MT5 page says execution is 'delivered from our Equinix LD4 facility server cluster' (London), the MT4 page says 'Equinix NY4/LD4', and the VPS page lists Equinix NY4 (New York) and LD4 (London). For MT5, latency to the actual server should be tested before choosing a VPS location; London looks the more likely.

EXECUTION MODEL: marketed as 'ECN pricing' with 'no dealing desk intervention or re quotes' (FAQ), market execution only. The ECN-pricing page itself says ECN pricing 'refers to how prices are determined' and 'is different from order execution', where a trade may be offset with a liquidity provider, matched with another client or held internally. The Saint Lucia client agreement says the company acts as agent, arranging execution with an execution venue / liquidity provider from which it receives monthly volume-based commissions (14.1, 42.1), while its execution policy (file dated 26 Jan 2026) names 'FP Markets Ltd' itself as the execution venue; the Seychelles policy (last update 16 Mar 2023) names the group company First Prudential Markets Pty Limited. All trades are OTC. This is aggregated-LP pricing with fills against an in-group venue, not a multilateral ECN. DailyForex's review adds that the broker 'may act as a market maker if it chooses or needs to do so'.

ORDER HANDLING AND SLIPPAGE RULES (client agreement Appendix A 2.3-2.16; execution policy 3.3): market orders are filled at the best available price, which may be higher or lower than the price shown; stop-loss, take-profit, limit and stop-entry orders are 'executed at first available market prices' and are 'not guaranteed' (FAQ: 'We are not able to guarantee stop losses'); negative slippage is filled at the next best price; for positive slippage the company 'can pass such price improvement on to the Client' (not an obligation); market orders that cannot be filled for lack of volume are cancelled; if the company cannot proceed with an order because of price or size it 'will send a re-quote' and the order is rejected (this contradicts the FAQ's no-requote wording); error quotes (spikes) are deleted from the server. The policy warns slippage is normal around news, session opens and illiquid periods, and the spreads page says spreads 'may widen significantly during volatile market conditions, causing slippage'. The MT5 page claims 'no minimum distance between orders and the current price' (stops level 0).

EXPERT ADVISORS AND SCALPING - marketing versus contract. Marketing: FAQ 'We do not have restrictions on using an Expert Advisor (EA)' and 'Do you allow scalping/hedging? Yes, we allow both strategies'; MT4/MT5 pages advertise 'Zero restrictions' and conditions 'optimised for scalping and Expert Advisors'. But (a) the FAQ caps account activity at 5,000 'movements' per 24 hours on the Saint Lucia site (10,000 on the Seychelles site), counting opened and closed trades, pending orders and every modification; a 'hyperactive' account is marked read-only and the client must contact support, which matters for an EA that trails stops tick by tick. (b) Both client agreements (14.14) say use of robots 'is expressly prohibited, unless you receive express written consent by the Company prior to activating the robot'. (c) 'Abusive Trading' (1.1) lists scalping, arbitrage, pip-hunting, gap-trading, leverage abuse and exploitation of faster/slower feeds; 'Scalping' is defined as opening 'too many positions in CFDs at the same time' and closing them 'for less than five minutes', or capturing the bid/ask difference; the client warrants not to trade for arbitrage or Scalping (26(j)); sanctions include cancelling profits, closing positions and terminating the account with only the first deposit returned (1.1, 25.1(o), 25.2(g)). No explicit minimum holding time is published beyond that five-minute definition. Written confirmation from support that the EA is permitted is advisable.

HEDGING / NETTING AND LIMITS: hedging is allowed (FAQ). FP Markets' MT5 guide says 'MT5 allows both hedging (on-demand / request) as well as netting', so the mode of a newly opened MT5 account is not unambiguous and should be read from ACCOUNT_MARGIN_MODE (the agreement refers to hedged margin and to stop-losses on 'lock positions'). Other limits: micro lots (0.01) on all MT4/MT5 account types; maximum 50 lots per forex trade; no cap on the number of open orders on live accounts, but the broker may merge positions when 500 or more are open (agreement 15.3); up to 10 trading accounts per client.

EXECUTION-QUALITY MEASUREMENTS: FP Markets publishes no slippage or fill statistics (its policy only mentions internal 'symmetric slippage checks'). Independent tests found: CompareForexBrokers 2026 test (EAs on MT4 demo accounts, 36 brokers, two 30-hour runs, ping subtracted): market orders 96 ms (8th of 36; the others average 151 ms), limit orders 225 ms (31st of 36; others 141 ms). FXEmpire on 27 April, MT5 demo just after the New York open: 522-635 ms (gold 626 ms), against the broker's claimed 40 ms average. WikiFX shows an average execution speed of 176.56 ms. All are demo or aggregate figures, not live Standard-account slippage; no measured slippage distribution was found for this broker.

USER REPORTS (Trustpilot: TrustScore 4.7 from 10,396 reviews on 2026-11-10; anecdotal and unverified): slippage complaints cluster on stop orders and news, for example the CPI release of 12 Jan 2023, 'up to 60 pips' on overnight holds (30 May 2023), 'unjustified slippage of 3 pips total per trade' on EUR/USD and GBP/USD copy trades (6 Jul 2025), and a sell-stop slippage that blew an account (11 Sep 2026). FP Markets' replies: 'as we offer Market execution, slippage can occur, especially while trading during high-impact economic events' (20 May 2024) and that slippage 'can occur due to market depth, execution latency' (23 Jul 2025). Many 5-star reviews report minimal slippage; no requote complaints were visible. Recent 1-2 star reviews (Jul-Oct 2026) concern cancelled profits or account restriction for 'abusive trading' (FP Markets replied citing its terms and a Financial Commission decision in its favour), a dispute over trades opened by an EA (5 Oct 2026), and slow withdrawals.

VPS: provided with partner Liquidity Connect in Equinix NY4/LD4. FP Markets covers the subscription when monthly volume exceeds 5 lots of Forex and Metals on a Standard MT4/MT5 account (10 lots on Raw; 20 and 40 on cTrader); traders new to VPS can be sponsored with 'a minimum deposit of US$1000 or equivalent' plus the volume requirement; only forex and metals volume counts, so index and crypto trades do not; it is requested by live chat or e-mail. The FAQ still quotes older thresholds (10 lots Standard / 20 Raw). An older FP Markets blog post, seen only as a search snippet, says the free VPS may be cancelled if the requirement is missed two months running. No price for a paid plan is shown on the VPS page (Coin Bureau quoted about US$25 a month in 2023). A EUR 1,000 account trading 0.01-0.05 lots may not reach 5 lots a month.

MINIMUM DEPOSIT: official FAQ: 'There is no minimum deposit; this depends on the payment method you choose' (MT5 page: 'No minimum deposit'). Third parties quote US$100 / AU$100 as the practical opening amount for Standard and Raw (WikiFX, DayTrading.com, Tradingpedia; CompareForexBrokers for the Seychelles company), and CompareForexBrokers observed a US$40 card minimum on 30 Oct 2026. EUR 1,000 is above every figure found.

ACCOUNT CURRENCIES: FAQ: 'You can open an account in AUD, USD, EUR, GBP, SGD, CAD, CHF, HKD, JPY and PLN', so EUR accounts are available on the global entities (the ASIC entity lists only AUD and USD). Reviewers list a few more (NZD, CZK, AED per FXEmpire; ZAR, MXN per CompareForexBrokers). The agreement says the broker does not convert client money between currencies (19.1); no published conversion fee for profit and loss on USD-quoted instruments in a EUR account was found.

STANDARD ACCOUNT COST STRUCTURE: zero commission on all MT4/MT5 instruments, cost built into the spread. FAQ: 'There is zero commission on the Standard account, with a 1 pip mark up on the spread.
